newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BIL may want larger Fairfax stake - Sir Ron.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BIL may want larger Fairfax stake - Sir Ron.

text.p: Sir Ron Brierley, founder and non-executive vice president of New Zealand based Brierley Investments Ltd, said on Tuesday the company could seek to increase its newly-acquired stake in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd depending on the outcome of the Australian government's cross-media ownership review.

"I think it's a possibility, yes," Brierley told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio when asked whether the company wanted a larger holding. "I think BIL would be looking to a larger shareholding if it was able to do that, if it was satisfied with what happens in respect of the existing shareholding."

Canadian media tycoon Conrad Black announced on Monday the sale of his 25 percent stake in Fairfax to BIL for a total of A$553.8 million. BIL is an investment group noted for taking strategic stakes in companies and then selling at a profit.
When asked if BIL would attempt to lift its stake only if the outcome of the media review meant it was unable to on-sell the holding, Brierley said: "I think that's possible, yes."
Black's move off the Fairfax share register is seen as clearing the way for Australian media baron Kerry Packer to take control of the newspaper publisher.
Moves by Packer are dependent on changes to the cross-media ownership rules as a result of the government review.

Packer holds 15 percent of Fairfax, but is not allowed to raise that stake because of his television holdings, although his Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd has said it would like to merge with Fairfax.

Brierley said that as far as he knew, BIL had not held any discussions with either Packer or News Corp Ltd chairman and chief executive Rupert Murdoch about the possibility of on-selling the Fairfax stake to one of them.
"I've only been involved in a non-executive capacity so I can't really vouch for the details, but I'm fairly sure the answer to that is no," he said.
